boundaryAudit.asked: The deployment's owner set four boundaries, each needing his decision before anything is built that crosses one: (1) new logic in the daemon beyond moving work through phases and keeping pods running, and any new control or constraint on agents; (2) any programmatic check on an agent's output; (3) any new requirement on the handoffs between roles; (4) any company- or deployment-specific logic in Legion itself.
clear: Boundary 3, no new handoff requirement. The `handoff_complete` request shape is unchanged; the contract diff is a doc comment and a note string on the response. Every role-prompt change is a deletion or a pagination flag. `record.ReadyMerge.warned` and `.queued` are a daemon-owned outbox payload's fields, which no role writes or reads.

Boundary 4, nothing deployment-specific. No file of the 76 names a deployment, and check-private-names.sh passes over 4,874 files. The only mention of a deployment repository anywhere in this change's record is a risk line in the pull request body, which the required lint reads through check-pr-text.sh and has passed at every head that carried it.

nearTheLine.argumentItIsClear: It adds no control over any agent and constrains nothing: it blocks no call, refuses no completion and changes no phase. nearTheLine.argumentItIsNear: Read literally, a timer that fires a notice an hour after a row is queued is new daemon logic beyond moving work through phases and keeping pods running. Nothing else in the daemon measures elapsed time to tell a human something.
nearTheLine.disposition: Reported to the architect for its decision, with this reasoning and no action taken. It is the change's central deliverable (the fifth), so removing it is a scope decision rather than a cleanup.
